title: The Gold Chain Grab on MG Road
scenario: Ramesh, while riding pillion on a motorcycle, quickly reaches out and violently snatches a gold chain from Sunita's neck as she crosses the street, immediately speeding away. Under IPC, this was charged under Section 379 (theft) or Section 392 (robbery). How is this charged under the BNS?
explanation: BNS Section 304 specifically creates a distinct statutory offence of 'Snatching' to bridge the gap between simple theft and violent robbery for street crimes.

title: Caste-Motivated Mob Attack
scenario: A group of six persons acting in concert brutally attacks and kills a man in a village solely on account of his caste and community affiliation. Under the new BNS, which provision directly penalizes this act with capital punishment or life imprisonment for every member?
options: BNS Section 103(1) general murder read with Section 3(5)
BNS Section 103(2) (Murder by group / Mob lynching on grounds of caste, race, sex, etc.)
explanation: BNS Section 103(2) is a brand-new sub-section specifically penalizing group murder / mob lynching on grounds of race, caste, community, sex, place of birth, or personal belief.

title: First-Time Shoplifting of a Book
scenario: A 19-year-old student steals a legal textbook worth ₹1,800 from a bookstore and is caught. This is his first offence, and he immediately restores the book. Under BNS Section 303(2), what unique sentencing option does the Magistrate now have that did not exist in IPC Section 379?
options: Community service upon return of the stolen property
Can only impose fine of at least ₹50,000
explanation: Under BNS Section 303(2) proviso, where stolen property value is under ₹5,000, and it is a first conviction upon return of property/value, community service may be awarded.

title: Social Media Defamation Post
scenario: An individual publishes an intentionally false and reputation-damaging allegation against a local merchant on social media. The trial court convicts him of defamation. Under BNS Section 356(2), what reformative punishment can the court now award alongside or instead of imprisonment and fine?
options: Bar from using internet for 5 years
explanation: BNS Section 356(2) replaces IPC 500 and explicitly incorporates 'community service' as an alternative punishment for defamation.

title: Doctor's Operating Room Complication
scenario: A patient dies following unforeseen complications during surgery performed by a certified surgeon. The family files a complaint of death by negligence. Under BNS Section 106(1), how is the punishment for registered medical practitioners treated compared to ordinary rash acts?
options: Doctor is immune from all criminal prosecution
Doctor's punishment is capped at 2 years, whereas ordinary death by negligence is up to 5 years
Doctor is punished under Section 103 for murder
explanation: While general death by negligence was raised from 2 to 5 years in BNS 106(1), doctors performing medical procedures are specifically capped at up to 2 years.

title: Online Financial Fraud by Phishing
scenario: Vikram creates a fake bank website and dishonestly induces Priya to transfer ₹2,50,000 to his account. In earlier days, FIRs routinely invoked IPC Section 420. Which corresponding section of the BNS should now be cited in the FIR?
explanation: IPC Section 420 (cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property) is now codified under BNS Section 318(4).

title: Matrimonial Cruelty Complaint
scenario: A woman files a complaint that her husband and mother-in-law subjected her to severe harassment over dowry demands. Under IPC, this was covered in Section 498A (offence and definition combined). Under BNS, how has this section been reorganized?
options: Split: Section 85 contains the offence/punishment, while Section 86 defines 'cruelty'
Shifted to the civil family courts exclusively
explanation: IPC Section 498A is split into two sections in BNS: Section 85 prescribes punishment (up to 3 years and fine) and Section 86 defines the dimensions of 'cruelty'.

title: Repeal of Sedition (Rajdroh)
scenario: A political activist delivers an anti-government speech criticizing official policy. Under the old IPC, police frequently registered charges under IPC Section 124A (Sedition). What is the status of 'sedition' in the BNS?
options: Retained with identical wording under Section 124
Sedition term is omitted; Section 152 penalizes acts endangering sovereignty, unity, and integrity with a higher threshold (secession/rebellion)
No offence against the state exists anymore
Sedition is now punished with only a small fine
explanation: The colonial offence of 'sedition' (rajdroh) was omitted. Section 152 of BNS targets acts endangering sovereignty, unity, or integrity of India through secession, armed rebellion, or subversive activities.

title: Syndicate Extortion and Land Grabbing
scenario: A criminal syndicate operates an extortion racket, running land-grabbing schemes and contract killings across district lines. Under IPC, prosecutors had to rely on state-specific enactments (like MCOCA) or multiple separate offences. Which new central provision in BNS tackles organized crime?
explanation: BNS Section 111 introduces a comprehensive central penal provision specifically addressing organized crime syndicates.

title: Unnatural Offences and Adult Consensual Acts
scenario: A police officer attempts to file an FIR under Section 377 for private consensual relations between two adults. The public prosecutor advises that the provision has changed. What happened to Section 377 IPC in the BNS?
options: It was renumbered as BNS Section 377 without change
It has been omitted from the BNS
The punishment was doubled to 20 years
It was moved to the Income Tax Act
explanation: IPC Section 377 has been omitted from the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, reflecting the Supreme Court's ruling in Navtej Singh Johar (2018).

title: Attempt to Murder in a Street Brawl
scenario: During a heated dispute, Karan stabs an unarmed victim in the chest with intent to kill, but timely surgical intervention saves the victim's life. What was IPC Section 307 renumbered to in the BNS?
explanation: Attempt to murder, previously the famous Section 307 IPC, is now Section 109 of the BNS.

title: Unlawful Assembly common intention vs common object
scenario: Five college students assemble outside a government office to forcibly prevent a public servant from entering. Which section defines this unlawful assembly in BNS (formerly IPC 141)?
explanation: The definition of unlawful assembly moved from IPC Section 141 to BNS Section 189(1).

title: Eve-Teasing and Indecent Gestures
scenario: A man utters sexually vulgar insults and makes obscene gestures at a woman standing at a bus stop. In IPC, this was charged under Section 509. Which section of BNS now protects the modesty of a woman against words and gestures?
explanation: IPC Section 509 is renumbered to Section 79 of BNS, positioned in Chapter V on offences against women and children.

title: Criminal Breach of Trust by Warehouse Manager
scenario: A warehouse manager entrusted with 1,000 laptops sells 200 of them on the black market for personal gain. Under IPC Section 406, the maximum imprisonment was 3 years. What is the maximum imprisonment under BNS Section 316(2)?
explanation: Under BNS Section 316(2), the maximum penalty for criminal breach of trust has been enhanced from 3 years to 5 years imprisonment.

title: Common Intention Rule Relocation
scenario: Three associates plan a bank heist and execute it together. The prosecution seeks to hold each liable for acts done in furtherance of common intention (formerly IPC Section 34). Where is this constructive liability principle located in BNS?
explanation: The common intention principle of IPC Section 34 is now codified as sub-section (5) of Section 3 in BNS.

title: Dowry Death Within Seven Years
scenario: A bride dies of burn injuries in her marital home 3 years after wedding following relentless harassment for a luxury car. Which section of BNS replaces IPC Section 304B?
explanation: IPC Section 304B has been shifted to Chapter V as Section 80 of BNS with the same 7-year statutory presumption.

title: Voyeurism via Hidden Cameras in Hotel
scenario: A hotel operator installs a hidden camera in a guest bathroom to record private acts without consent. Which BNS section replaces IPC Section 354C for voyeurism?
explanation: Voyeurism moves from IPC Section 354C to BNS Section 77 without altering penal limits.

title: Rash and Negligent Driving
scenario: A driver speeds recklessly through a busy market at 90 km/h, endangering pedestrians. In IPC, this was registered under Section 279. Which section of BNS applies?
explanation: Rash driving or riding on a public way moves from IPC Section 279 to Section 281 of BNS.
chapter: Offences Affecting Public Health, Safety, and Decency

title: Criminal Intimidation and Death Threats
scenario: An extortionist calls a businessman and threatens to shoot his children if he does not pay money within 24 hours. Under IPC, this was Section 506. Under BNS, which section penalizes criminal intimidation?
explanation: Criminal intimidation is defined in BNS Section 351(1) and punished under BNS Section 351(2).

title: Hit and Run Escape
scenario: A driver causes the death of a pedestrian through rash driving and immediately flees the scene without reporting to police or a magistrate. Under BNS Section 106(2), what is the maximum imprisonment he faces?
explanation: BNS Section 106(2) creates a dedicated aggravated hit-and-run offence carrying imprisonment up to 10 years and fine for escaping after causing death.

scenario: A foreign national located in Dubai hacks into a financial server located in Mumbai, corrupting banking records. When questioned on jurisdiction, the prosecutor invokes BNS Section 1. Does the BNS apply to this cyber offence committed outside India?
options: No, BNS only applies within India's physical land borders
Yes, Section 1(5)(c) expressly applies to any person targeting computer resources located in India
Only if the offender is an Indian citizen holding an Indian passport
No, only the Information Technology Act can apply
answer: Yes, Section 1(5)(c) expressly applies to any person targeting computer resources located in India
explanation: BNS Section 1(5)(c) explicitly extends extraterritorial jurisdiction to any person in any place without and beyond India committing any offence targeting a computer resource located in India.

scenario: In a criminal trial involving digital evidence, the defence argues that an encrypted instant message chat does not qualify as a 'document' under the penal law. How does BNS Section 2 resolve this?
options: Digital records are not considered documents under criminal law
Section 2(8) consolidates definitions and explicitly includes electronic and digital records as documents
Only paper documents with physical wax seals qualify
Only messages sent via government postal services qualify
answer: Section 2(8) consolidates definitions and explicitly includes electronic and digital records as documents
explanation: BNS Section 2(8) defines 'document' to expressly include electronic and digital records, emails, server logs, and messages stored on digital devices.

scenario: Four individuals plan a warehouse robbery. Two break open the gates while the other two stand guard outside with weapons. One guard shoots a night watchman. Where is the principle of joint constructive liability codified in BNS?
explanation: The principle of common intention (formerly IPC Section 34) is now codified under BNS Section 3(5), holding each participant liable for acts done in furtherance of the common intention.

scenario: A judicial magistrate convicts a first-time offender for an altercation involving minor public misconduct. Wishing to avoid sending the youth to jail, the magistrate sentences him to clean a public park for 10 hours. Under which section of BNS is this penalty recognized?
options: BNS Section 4, which adds 'Community service' as a statutory punishment
Magistrates have no power to award community service
answer: BNS Section 4, which adds 'Community service' as a statutory punishment
explanation: BNS Section 4 introduces 'Community service' as the sixth formal statutory category of punishment alongside death, imprisonment for life, imprisonment, forfeiture, and fine.

scenario: A court is calculating the fractional sentence for an attempt to commit an offence punishable with life imprisonment. Under BNS Section 6, how many years is imprisonment for life reckoned as for fraction calculations?
explanation: BNS Section 6 (formerly IPC Section 57) provides that in calculating fractions of terms of punishment, imprisonment for life shall be reckoned as equivalent to imprisonment for twenty years.

scenario: An accused is convicted of an offence carrying a maximum prison term of 4 years and fine. The magistrate sentences him to 1 year imprisonment and a fine of ₹10,000, with default imprisonment of 2 years if unpaid. Is this default sentence lawful under BNS Section 8?
options: Yes, default imprisonment can be of any length at the magistrate's discretion
No, under Section 8(3), default imprisonment cannot exceed one-fourth of the maximum term (1 year max)
Yes, provided it does not exceed 3 years
No, fine defaults can only be punished with community service
answer: No, under Section 8(3), default imprisonment cannot exceed one-fourth of the maximum term (1 year max)
explanation: Under BNS Section 8(3) (formerly IPC 65), the term of imprisonment in default of payment of fine shall not exceed one-fourth of the maximum term of imprisonment fixed for the offence.

scenario: A 6-year-old child picks up a gold coin from a neighbour's table and puts it into his pocket. The neighbour seeks to lodge a police complaint for theft under Section 303 BNS. What statutory defence applies?
options: BNS Section 20: absolute immunity under 7 years of age (doli incapax)
No defence; the child must be tried in juvenile court
answer: BNS Section 20: absolute immunity under 7 years of age (doli incapax)
explanation: BNS Section 20 (formerly IPC Section 82) provides that nothing is an offence which is done by a child under seven years of age (doli incapax).

scenario: An unconscious accident victim with severe internal bleeding is rushed to the hospital. A surgeon performs an immediate emergency laparotomy to save the victim's life without waiting for relatives' consent. Which section of BNS protects the surgeon from criminal liability?
options: BNS Section 30 (act done in good faith for person's benefit without consent in emergency)
answer: BNS Section 30 (act done in good faith for person's benefit without consent in emergency)
explanation: BNS Section 30 (formerly IPC Section 92) provides that nothing is an offence done in good faith for the benefit of a person even without consent when obtaining consent is impossible in an emergency.

scenario: At 2:00 AM, a homeowner wakes up to find an armed intruder breaking through the bedroom window carrying a sharp machete and threatening to kill anyone who moves. The homeowner shoots the intruder, causing death. Which section justifies this act?
options: BNS Section 41 (right of private defence of property against night house-breaking extends to causing death)
answer: BNS Section 41 (right of private defence of property against night house-breaking extends to causing death)
explanation: Under BNS Section 41 (formerly IPC Section 103), the right of private defence of property extends to voluntary causing of death in cases of house-breaking by night or robbery.

scenario: A cyber-criminal residing in Country X sends remote malicious code and instructions to an operative in New Delhi to hack a power grid inside India. Under IPC, prosecuting foreign abettors was procedurally complex. Which newly introduced section of BNS explicitly penalizes abetment outside India for an offence inside India?
options: BNS Section 48 (Abetment outside India for offence in India)
answer: BNS Section 48 (Abetment outside India for offence in India)
explanation: Section 48 of BNS is a newly enacted provision that explicitly criminalizes a person who, outside and beyond India, abets the commission of any act within India that would constitute an offence.

scenario: A instigates B to burn down Z's empty barn at midnight. While burning the barn, B also takes the opportunity to steal jewellery from a nearby farmhouse without A's knowledge or expectation. Is A liable for the jewellery theft as an abettor?
options: No, because under BNS Section 51 an abettor is liable for a different act only if it was a probable consequence of the abetment
Yes, an abettor is strictly liable for every single crime the perpetrator commits that night
Yes, under Section 61 for criminal conspiracy
No, because burning a barn is not an offence under BNS
answer: No, because under BNS Section 51 an abettor is liable for a different act only if it was a probable consequence of the abetment
explanation: Under BNS Section 51 (formerly IPC 111), when an act is abetted and a different act is done, the abettor is liable for the divergent act only if it was a probable consequence of the abetment.

scenario: Three persons agree in a private room to commit armed bank dacoity next month, but are arrested before taking any physical steps towards the bank. Are they guilty of criminal conspiracy, and under which section are definition and punishment now consolidated?
options: Guilty under BNS Section 61 (merging IPC 120A definition and IPC 120B punishment into one section)
Not guilty, because no overt physical act has occurred
Guilty only under BNS Section 62 for attempt
Not guilty, because an agreement alone can never constitute an offence
answer: Guilty under BNS Section 61 (merging IPC 120A definition and IPC 120B punishment into one section)
explanation: Under BNS Section 61 (consolidating IPC 120A and 120B), an agreement to commit a serious offence punishable with rigorous imprisonment of 2+ years constitutes criminal conspiracy without requiring any overt act.

scenario: A man creates a fake profile concealing his true religious identity and marital status, promises to marry a woman, engages in sexual intercourse with her, and subsequently abandons her after securing his promotion. Under the old IPC, this was litigated under rape (s. 375/90) or cheating (s. 417). Which new section of BNS specifically penalizes this conduct?
options: BNS Section 69 (Sexual intercourse by employing deceitful means or false promise of marriage)
answer: BNS Section 69 (Sexual intercourse by employing deceitful means or false promise of marriage)
explanation: BNS Section 69 is a landmark new provision explicitly criminalizing sexual intercourse by deceitful means (including false promise of employment, promotion, or marriage after concealing identity) with imprisonment up to 10 years and fine.

scenario: A 17-year-old girl is gang-raped by three men acting in furtherance of a common intention. Under BNS Section 70(2), what is the mandatory punishment prescribed for each perpetrator?
options: Imprisonment for life (remainder of natural life) and fine, or death
Imprisonment for not less than 7 years extending to 10 years
Rigorous imprisonment for 10 years and fine
answer: Imprisonment for life (remainder of natural life) and fine, or death
explanation: BNS Section 70(2) significantly expanded the minor threshold to all females under 18 years of age, prescribing imprisonment for the remainder of natural life or the death penalty for every member of the group.

scenario: An adult gang leader recruits and pays a 13-year-old child to transport illicit firearms and contraband across state checkpoints. Which newly introduced section of BNS punishes hiring or engaging a child to commit an offence?
options: BNS Section 95 (Hiring, employing or engaging a child to commit an offence)
answer: BNS Section 95 (Hiring, employing or engaging a child to commit an offence)
explanation: BNS Section 95 is a brand-new offence specifically penalizing anyone who hires, employs, or engages a child to commit crimes or in sexual exploitation/child pornography, prescribing 3 to 10 years imprisonment, fine, and liability as if the adult committed the crime personally.
